body.text: ESCALATING UNREST ACROSS PAKISTAN-ADMINISTERED AZAD KASHMIR

The United Kashmir People's National Party (UKPNP) has unreservedly condemned the escalating use of force and extrajudicial killings across Pakistan-administered Azad Kashmir, urging an immediate halt to security force operations in Kotli, Rawalakot, and surrounding districts.

In an expansive statement issued on Wednesday, the party called for an urgent end to the regional communications blackout, the unconditional release of detained civil society members, and an independent judicial probe into ongoing casualties.
The digital siege has cut off millions of Azad Kashmir state subjects residing across the United Kingdom, Europe, North America, and the Middle East, leaving the global diaspora in deep distress.

According to the UKPNP, the latest wave of unrest stems from a targeted attack on June 5 near Barmanag Khaigala, which left Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) Core Committee member Umar Nazir Kashmiri severely wounded and resulted in the death of his close associate and media adviser, Shahzaib Habib.

items: CMH Rawalakot Incident: On June 7, security forces opened fire on mourners and demonstrators gathered outside the Combined Military Hospital (CMH) in Rawalakot to collect Habib's body for burial, resulting in at least 11 civilian deaths and scores of injuries.
Spreading Clashes in Kotli: Live-fire confrontations between security forces and civilian crowds have spread to Kotli and neighboring areas, triggering additional casualties amid an expanding curfew.
Mass Arrests and Disappearances: Hundreds of local residents and activists have reportedly been arbitrarily detained, with families receiving no official confirmation of their whereabouts.

body.text: BROKEN AGREEMENTS AND DUPLICITY IN NEGOTIATIONS

The UKPNP highlighted a pattern of broken state pledges, citing previous lethal crackdowns in Muzaffarabad in 2024 and October 2025. Although federal ministers and local Azad Kashmir authorities engaged in high-level talks with JAAC leadership in Muzaffarabad as recently as late May 2026, the Home Department subsequently issued a notification on June 5 proscribing the civil rights coalition as a 'terrorist organization' under the Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA) of 2014.

The party characterized the proscription as a draconian abuse of anti-terror legislation designed to criminalize legitimate democratic dissent. Alongside military deployments, authorities enforced a total telecommunications, broadband, and media blackout across Rawalakot, Kotli, and adjacent territories.
The UKPNP called on the Government of Pakistan to immediately implement key corrective measures to protect civilian lives and restore stability:

items: Cease Hostilities: Immediately halt all military and paramilitary operations, tactical drone usage, and live ammunition deployment against peaceful civilians.
Revoke Proscription & Resume Dialogue: Lift the ban on the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) and return to negotiations to resolve socio-economic and political demands.
Ensure Accountability for Detainees: Produce all arrested individuals before transparent legal authorities, end ill-treatment, and facilitate their unconditional release.
Provide Medical Access: Guarantee immediate, non-discriminatory healthcare for all injured individuals without fear of arrest or harassment.
Restore Communications: Re-establish full internet, mobile, and landline services across the entire territory.
Initiate Judicial Inquiry: Launch an independent judicial investigation into the killings in Rawalakot, Kotli, and across Azad Kashmir.

body.text: The UKPNP warned against any attempts to use emergency measures as a pretext for administrative restructuring, including declaring the region a federal territory or merging it into Pakistani provinces. The party reiterated its appeal to the United Nations, European Union, United States, and international community to intervene directly to protect civilian lives and fundamental rights.
